characterList.name: Kevin Powell

content_metadata.description: This video addresses a common issue in web development where anchor links cause content to be hidden behind fixed navigation bars. Kevin Powell introduces a CSS-based solution and further refines it using JavaScript for enhanced robustness.

qAndA.question: What CSS property is used to make the navigation bar sticky?
What value is used for the 'z-index' of the navigation bar?
What is the initial fallback value used for the 'scroll-padding-top' property?
What JavaScript method is used to set the custom property for the scroll padding?

qAndA.answer: The issue is that the calculated navigation height won't automatically be recalculated if the navigation bar changes size.
qAndA.question: What potential issue is mentioned regarding resizing the browser window?

Kevin explains the problem of the navigation bar overlapping content.
Kevin introduces the 'scroll-padding-top' property as a solution.

Kevin uses JavaScript to set a custom property with the navigation bar's height.
Kevin fixes a bug where he was adding instead of subtracting a pixel.

youtube_description:
When we have a fixed navigation with anchor links that go to different locations within the page, that navigation can cover content when it scrolls to that location on the page. Luckily, it's easy to fix with some scroll-padding!

🔗 Links 
✅ The CodePen: https://codepen.io/kevinpowell/pen/GRQyZMX
✅ More position sticky stuff: https://youtu.be/8TyoihVGErI
